description:
Reflect the foundation identity-seam decision (JMAP-ga0q) in the workspace's authoritative AGENTS.md and PLAN.md files.

## Sites to update

### workspace AGENTS.md (/home/mark/PROJECT/JMAP/AGENTS.md)

Add a new top-level section 'Caller identity (foundation seam)' after the existing 'TLS stack' bullet, with the following rules:

  - `JmapBackend::principal_id(&Self::CallerCtx) -> Option<&jmap_types::Id>` is the ONLY way the JMAP layer asks 'who is the caller'.
  - **Backends are canonical for permission enforcement.** Handlers do NO permission checking. Defense-in-depth handler-side pre-checks are allowed but the backend MUST re-verify atomically with the mutation.
  - Identity is a foundation concept. Future extensions that need richer caller info (groups, claims, roles) add it to their OWN backend trait, NOT to `JmapBackend`. Foundation provides the id; extensions own the meaning.
  - Federation does NOT bypass this seam — the federation handler maps peer identity to a local principal once, before invoking the JMAP method. JMAP method code sees a normal `principal_id()`.
  - Returning `None` from `principal_id` is a deliberate deployment choice signifying 'this server does not honor identity-dependent JMAP semantics'.

### crate-jmap-server/AGENTS.md

Update the 'Design Constraints — Settled — Do Not Revisit' table row 'Auth' from:
  'Not in dispatcher | Caller's responsibility — do it before `dispatch()`'
to:
  'HTTP layer authenticates; JMAP layer reads caller via `JmapBackend::principal_id` | Foundation provides the identity seam; backends decide what to do with it. Handler-side permission gates are FORBIDDEN — backends are canonical.'

### crate-jmap-server/PLAN.md

Document the principal_id method in the public-API section with cross-references to consumer beads (JMAP-g7wu.2.4 chat Space/set as first consumer; future: jmap-mail-server $seen on shared mailboxes, jmap-calendars-server ACLs, jmap-sharing-server myRights, jmap-metadata-server isPrivate scoping).

### crate-jmap-chat-server/AGENTS.md

Add a new section 'Permission enforcement: backend canonical' documenting:
  - All Space/set permission gates live in `MemoryBackend::apply_space_patch` (or the equivalent in real backends).
  - Handler `handle_space_set` does NOT permission-check.
  - The `required_permissions_for_op(&SpacePatchOp) -> &'static [&'static str]` helper (filed under JMAP-g7wu.2.4.10 if numbered there) is pure and may be consumed by any backend; the GATING using it is backend-side only.

## Acceptance

  - All four files updated with the verbatim text above (or close paraphrase preserving the normative content).
  - No code changes — docs only.
  - `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` clean.
  - The phrase 'handler-side permission gates are forbidden' appears in crate-jmap-server/AGENTS.md so future contributors hit it on first read.

## Depends on

JMAP-ga0q.1 (method must exist before docs reference it).
title: Document identity-seam policy in workspace AGENTS.md files
